skip: The saved article has about 200 words of text, too little for 260 words without padding. It would add: the site lies some 25 km north-east of Zeerust in the Tshwenyane hills; archaeologists estimate it was founded in the late 1400s on iron and copper ore deposits; it was sacked in 1821 by the Batlokwa under Mantatisi and attacked again about 1823 by Sebetwane and the Bafokeng, the survivors fleeing west to the Bakwena; the ruins were declared a National Heritage Site in 2011; the name is thought to come from a Tswana phrase about baboons; Campbell's 'Kurreechane' survives in the names of the Kurrichane thrush and buttonquail. NB the article gives Campbell's 1820 population as 20,000, the entry 16,000.
